definition: The energy a body has because it is moving, $E_\text{k} = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \frac{p^{2}}{2m}$; a scalar that is never negative, measured in joules.
The energy a body has because of its position in a gravitational field; close to Earth's surface its change is $\Delta E_\text{p} = mg\Delta h$, with $\Delta h$ the vertical change in height.
The energy stored in a stretched or compressed body such as a spring; for a spring obeying Hooke's law it is $E_\text{H} = \tfrac{1}{2}k(\Delta x)^{2}$.
The sum of a system's kinetic, gravitational potential and elastic potential energy; it stays constant when only weight and spring forces do work, with no friction, air resistance or driving force.
